'''Che Chi-ming''' ({{zh|c=支志明|p=Zhī Zhìmíng}}; born 7 September 1957), is a Hong Kong chemist currently holding [[Zhou Guangzhao]] Professorship in Natural Sciences, following a Dr. Hui Wai-Haan's Chair of Chemistry at the [[University of Hong Kong]] (HKU). In 1995, he became the first scientist from Hong Kong to be elected as a member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=:0>{{cite web
|title=Professor CHE, Chi Ming
|series=Teaching Staff
|url=https://www.scifac.hku.hk/people/che-chi-ming
|publisher=Faculty of Science, [[The University of Hong Kong]]
|access-date=17 June 2024
}}</ref> As of today, he remains the youngest academician of the CAS ever to be elected. He is known for extensive work in [[inorganic chemistry]], [[photochemistry]], and [[medicinal chemistry]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/chi-ming-che-gcfvgd/|title=Chi-Ming Che|website=www.nasonline.org|access-date=2017-06-05}}</ref>

== Career ==
Che received his B.S. degree at HKU in 1978.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ashk.org.hk/en/ourMembers/details/34|title=Chi-Ming CHE - Our Members |website=The Academy of Sciences of Hong Kong|access-date=2017-06-05}}</ref> He then received his Ph. D degree in inorganic chemistry at HKU working under Professor Chung-Kwong Poon in 1980. After earning his Ph. D., he spent 3 years at the [[California Institute of Technology]] conducting research in organometallic and [[bioinorganic chemistry]] in the laboratory of [[Harry B. Gray]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.facs-as.org/a77.html|title=Prof. Chi-Ming Che - Federation of Asian Chemical Societies|website=www.facs-as.org|access-date=2017-06-05}}</ref>

Following his research stay in the United States, Che moved back to Hong Kong and started his independent career as a faculty at HKU. During the past 20 years, he has also held visiting lecturer positions at [[National Taiwan University]], [[Jilin University]], and [[Sun Yat-sen University]]. Moreover, he has been a professor at [[Nanjing University]], [[Nankai University]], and [[Tsinghua University]]; and an honorary professor at [[Huazhong University of Science and Technology]], [[Northeast Normal University]], Nanjing University, and other universities.<ref name=":0" />

In 2007, he was elected as a member of [[The World Academy of Sciences]] (TWAS) in Chemical Sciences. In 2013, he was elected as a foreign associate of the United States [[National Academy of Sciences]].

Currently, he is the Zhou Guangzhao Professorship in Natural Sciences and Chair of Chemistry, Department of Chemistry, Faculty of Science, the [[University of Hong Kong]].<ref name=:0/>

In December 2021, it was reported that Che was eligible to vote four times in the [[2021 Hong Kong legislative election]], yielding 0.0459334% of the total voting value (elected seats), which is 9242 times more than the value of an average voter's total voting value.<ref>{{Cite web|last=FactWire|date=2021-12-15|title=Factwire: 41 privileged voters have 7,200 times greater power than a regular Hong Kong voter following election revamp|url=https://hongkongfp.com/2021/12/16/factwire-41-privileged-voters-have-7200-times-greater-power-than-a-regular-hong-kong-voter-following-election-revamp/|access-date=2021-12-16|website=Hong Kong Free Press HKFP|language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Research ==
[[File:Epoxidation_and_Cyclopropanation_of_Alkene_Based_on_Using_Ru(III)_Catalyst.jpg|thumb|Ruthenium(III) porphyrin functionalized with PEG group is used as a catalyst to drive selective pathway of alkene to epoxide or cyclopropane.]]
[[File:Structure_of_PEGylated_Gold(III)_Conjugates.jpg|thumb|Structure of PEGylated Gold(III) Conjugates]]
Che's research interests cover various areas in chemistry such as [[inorganic chemistry]], [[materials science]], [[photochemistry]], and [[biomedical sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://croucher.org.hk/professor-che-chi-ming|title=Professor CHE Chi Ming {{!}} Croucher Foundation|website=croucher.org.hk|date=19 May 2011 |language=en-US|access-date=2017-06-05}}</ref> He has been engaged in inorganic chemistry research, [[Organometallic chemistry|organometallic]] synthesis where he and his group have studied high-valent and multimetallic complexes.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Che|first1=Chi Ming.|last2=Cheng|first2=Wing Kin.|date=1986-07-01|title=Novel UV-vis spectral feature and electrochemical behavior of high-valent osmium(VI) dioxo complex of 1,4,8,11-tetramethyl-1,4,8,11-tetraazacyclotetradecane (TMC). Reversible three-electron redox couple and vibronic structured UV-vis absorption bands involving trans-[Os(VI)(TMC)O2]2+|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=108|issue=15|pages=4644–4645|doi=10.1021/ja00275a062|issn=0002-7863}}</ref> These molecules have been investigated for their luminescent and catalytic properties. Notable systems that Che has developed include: catalysts for asymmetric olefin [[epoxidation]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last1=Chan|first1=Wing-Kei|last2=Liu|first2=Peng|last3=Yu|first3=Wing-Yiu|last4=Wong|first4=Man-Kin|last5=Che|first5=Chi-Ming|date=2004-05-01|title=Highly Diastereoselective Epoxidation of Allyl-Substituted Cycloalkenes Catalyzed by Metalloporphyrins|journal=Organic Letters|volume=6|issue=10|pages=1597–1599|doi=10.1021/ol0496475|pmid=15128245|issn=1523-7060}}</ref> [[Biomimetics|biomimetic]] oxidation catalyst featuring recognition elements, and molecular devices based on [[Luminescence|luminescent]] materials.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cheng|first1=Gang|last2=So|first2=Gary Kwok-Ming|last3=To|first3=Wai-Pong|last4=Chen|first4=Yong|last5=Kwok|first5=Chi-Chung|last6=Ma|first6=Chensheng|last7=Guan|first7=Xiangguo|last8=Chang|first8=Xiaoyong|last9=Kwok|first9=Wai-Ming|date=2015-07-14|title=Luminescent zinc(II) and copper(I) complexes for high-performance solution-processed monochromic and white organic light-emitting devices|journal=Chemical Science|volume=6|issue=8|pages=4623–4635|doi=10.1039/C4SC03161J|pmid=29142704|issn=2041-6539|pmc=5667404}}</ref>

=== Triplet Emitters ===
Che is a pioneer for the chemistry of d8 and d10 metal complexes including their excited state chemistry and closed shell metal-metal interactions of d8 and d10 metal ions.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.ashk.org.hk/en/ourMembers/details/34 |title = Chi-Ming CHE - Our Members - the Hong Kong Academy of Sciences 香港科學院}}</ref> His team has successfully developed practical tetradentate platinum(II)<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cheng |first1=Gang |last2=Kwak |first2=Yoonhyun |last3=To |first3=Wai-Pong |last4=Lam |first4=Tsz-Lung |last5=Tong |first5=Glenna So Ming |last6=Sit |first6=Man-Ki |last7=Gong |first7=Shaolong |last8=Choi |first8=Byoungki |last9=Choi |first9=Wha il |last10=Yang |first10=Chuluo |last11=Che |first11=Chi-Ming |title=High-Efficiency Solution-Processed Organic Light-Emitting Diodes with Tetradentate Platinum(II) Emitters |journal=ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces |date=13 November 2019 |volume=11 |issue=48 |pages=45161–45170 |doi=10.1021/acsami.9b11715|pmid=31718137 |s2cid=207962058 }}</ref> and gold(III)<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zhou |first1=Dongling |last2=To |first2=Wai-Pong |last3=Tong |first3=Glenna So Ming |last4=Cheng |first4=Gang |last5=Du |first5=Lili |last6=Phillips |first6=David Lee |last7=Che |first7=Chi-Ming |title=Luminescent Tetradentate Gold(III)-TADF Emitters: Microwave-Assisted Synthesis and High Performance OLEDs With EQEs Up To 25 % and Long Operational Lifetime |journal=Angewandte Chemie |date=15 January 2020 |doi=10.1002/ange.201914661|s2cid=243070975 }}</ref> Emitters which are comparable if not superior in performances to the World best Iridium(III) Phosphors

=== Metal Catalysts ===
Che has pioneered the developed of Ru-OXO system which has opened up numerous opportunities for efficient catalytic oxidation processes.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Che|first1=Chi Ming|last2=Yam|first2=Vivian Wing Wah|date=1987-02-01|title=Model complexes for the cis-ruthenium(VI)-dioxo system. Novel chemistry of [RuIII(N4O)(OH2)][ClO4]2 (N4OH = bis[2-(2-pyridyl)ethyl][2-hydroxy-2-(2-pyridyl)ethyl]amine)|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=109|issue=4|pages=1262–1263|doi=10.1021/ja00238a055|issn=0002-7863}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Che|first1=Chi-Ming|last2=Ho|first2=Clare|last3=Lau|first3=Tai-Chu|date=1991-01-01|title=Tuning the reactivities of ruthenium–oxo complexes with robust ligands. A ruthenium(IV)–oxo complex of 6,6′-dichloro-2,2′-bipyridine as an active oxidant for stoichiometric and catalytic organic oxidation|url=http://xlink.rsc.org/?DOI=DT9910001901|journal=J. Chem. Soc., Dalton Trans.|issue=8|pages=1901–1907|doi=10.1039/dt9910001901|issn=1364-5447|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Furthermore, Che and co-workers developed new methods for epoxidation, [[cyclopropanation]], and [[aziridination]] of alkenes.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last1=Zhang|first1=Jun-Long|last2=Che|first2=Chi-Ming|date=2002-05-01|title=Soluble Polymer-Supported Ruthenium Porphyrin Catalysts for Epoxidation, Cyclopropanation, and Aziridination of Alkenes|journal=Organic Letters|volume=4|issue=11|pages=1911–1914|doi=10.1021/ol0259138|pmid=12027645|issn=1523-7060}}</ref> His work on bioinorganic chemistry, has produced new understanding for several important processes including modern [[nitrogen fixation]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Che|first1=Chi-Ming|last2=Lam|first2=Hon-Wah|last3=Tong|first3=Wai-Fong|last4=Lai|first4=Ting-Fong|last5=Lau|first5=Tai-Chu|date=1989-01-01|title=Model reactions for nitrogen fixation. Photo-induced formation and X-ray crystal structure of [Os2(NH3)8(MeCN)2(N2)]5+ from [OsVI(NH3)4N]3+|url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/Content/ArticleLanding/1989/C3/c39890001883|journal=Journal of the Chemical Society, Chemical Communications|issue=24|pages=1883–1884|doi=10.1039/C39890001883|issn=0022-4936|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

=== Anti-Cancer Metal Complexes ===
Another notable work from Che's group has been the development of gold-, platinum-, ruthenium- and palladium based metal compounds with [[anti-tumor]] activity.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zou |first1=Taotao |last2=Lum |first2=Ching Tung |last3=Lok |first3=Chun-Nam |last4=Zhang |first4=Jing-Jing |last5=Che |first5=Chi-Ming |title=Chemical biology of anticancer gold( ) and gold( ) complexes |journal=Chemical Society Reviews |date=2015 |volume=44 |issue=24 |pages=8786–8801 |doi=10.1039/C5CS00132C|pmid=25868756 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zou |first1=Taotao |last2=Lok |first2=Chun-Nam |last3=Wan |first3=Pui-Ki |last4=Zhang |first4=Zhi-Feng |last5=Fung |first5=Sin-Ki |last6=Che |first6=Chi-Ming |title=Anticancer metal-N-heterocyclic carbene complexes of gold, platinum and palladium |journal=Current Opinion in Chemical Biology |date=April 2018 |volume=43 |pages=30–36 |doi=10.1016/j.cbpa.2017.10.014|pmid=29136524 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Che |first1=Chi-Ming |last2=Siu |first2=Fung-Ming |title=Metal complexes in medicine with a focus on enzyme inhibition |journal=Current Opinion in Chemical Biology |date=April 2010 |volume=14 |issue=2 |pages=255–261 |doi=10.1016/j.cbpa.2009.11.015|pmid=20018553 }}</ref> Specifically, they found that [[Pegylated|PEGylated]] gold(III) conjugates can exhibit multifunctional properties and undergo selective delivery to tumor tissues. Importantly, some of these compounds do not exhibit harmful [[cytotoxicity]] to normal cells, as many Pt-based anti-cancer agents do.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/312015637|title=A multi-functional PEGylated gold( iii ) compound: potent anti-cancer properties and self-assembly into nanostructures for drug co-delivery|website=ResearchGate|access-date=2017-06-05}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lum|first1=Ching Tung|last2=Liu|first2=Xiong|last3=Sun|first3=Raymond Wai-Yin|last4=Li|first4=Xiang-Ping|last5=Peng|first5=Ying|last6=He|first6=Ming-Liang|last7=Kung|first7=Hsiang Fu|last8=Che|first8=Chi-Ming|last9=Lin|first9=Marie C. M.|date=2010-08-28|title=Gold(III) porphyrin 1a inhibited nasopharyngeal carcinoma metastasis in vivo and inhibited cell migration and invasion in vitro|journal=Cancer Letters|volume=294|issue=2|pages=159–166|doi=10.1016/j.canlet.2010.01.033|issn=1872-7980|pmid=20163914}}</ref>

== Notable awards ==

* 2006 First Class Prize of the State Natural Science Award of China
* 2006 [[TWAS Prize]] in chemistry from the Academy of Sciences for the Developing World
* 2013 [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (RSC) Centenary Prize
